title: Cross-Sentence Reasoning
summary: Teach Raawi that reviewer decisions often require multiple sentences, multiple speakers, multiple actions, or the full scene instead of a single isolated sentence.
learningObjectives: Understand that a harmless sentence can become meaningful when later text is read.
Connect previous dialogue, following dialogue, narration, scene descriptions, actions, objects, locations, and relationships.
Accumulate evidence across the scene before reaching a conclusion.
Avoid evaluating any sentence in complete isolation.

definitions.finding: A supported conclusion grounded in evidence across one or more sentences.
definitions.evidence: Literal text, action, narration, or context that supports a reviewer conclusion.
definitions.context: The surrounding material that changes or clarifies the meaning of a sentence.
definitions.crossSentenceReasoning: Connecting multiple sentences to understand the full meaning of a scene.
definitions.scene: A continuous unit of action, dialogue, or description in the screenplay.
definitions.intent: The purpose, direction, or meaning created by the surrounding scene.

reviewerPrinciples: A sentence may appear harmless on its own.
Later sentences can reveal the real intent.
Never evaluate a sentence in complete isolation.
Connect dialogue, narration, actions, objects, locations, and character relationships before judging.
reviewerMethodology: Read the current sentence in the context of the previous and following sentences.
Identify who is speaking and who is being addressed.
Check whether narration, dialogue, or scene description changes the meaning.
Look for actions or objects that confirm or contradict the sentence.
Only then decide whether the sentence supports a finding.
reasoningProcess: Expand to the surrounding dialogue and narration.
Check whether a later sentence reveals a hidden intent.
Merge sentence-level signals into one scene-level interpretation.
Judge the scene, not the isolated line.

minimum: A single sentence may be enough only if it is explicit and self-contained.
strong: Two or more sentences reinforce the same interpretation.
Actions or objects confirm the spoken line.
weak: A line that could mean more than one thing.
A sentence that only becomes suspicious after context.
insufficient: Guessing based on one sentence alone.
Assuming intent before reading the scene.
Ignoring later dialogue that changes the meaning.
confidenceGuidance: Low: only one sentence or no corroboration.
Medium: multiple sentences support the same direction.
High: dialogue, action, and context align.
Very High: dialogue, action, objects, and intent all align.

contextRules: Later dialogue may change the meaning of earlier dialogue.
Narration may explain or contradict what a character says.
Scene descriptions may reveal intent through objects, movement, or location.
Another character may confirm or contradict the apparent meaning.
The ending of the scene may reverse the interpretation of the beginning.
sceneLevelReasoning: Determine the purpose of the entire scene before deciding.
Ask whether the scene is building tension, revealing a plan, or resolving it.
Treat the scene as one narrative unit when necessary.
Use the whole scene to resolve ambiguity.
characterRelationshipAnalysis: Check whether one character is instructing, threatening, helping, or deceiving another.
Use relationships to understand whether an exchange is literal, cooperative, or concealed.
A relationship may explain why a harmless sentence later becomes suspicious.
crossSentenceReasoning: Sentence 1 may set up an ordinary situation.
Sentence 2 may reveal the true intent.
Sentence 3 may confirm the meaning through action or object use.
Never finalize meaning before reading the full local exchange.
crossSceneReasoning: Earlier scenes can create context for a later line.
A later scene can prove that an earlier line had a hidden meaning.
Do not freeze a conclusion before checking scene progression.
confidenceRules: One sentence alone usually means low confidence.
Dialogue plus action raises confidence further.
Dialogue plus action plus objects plus intent yields very high confidence.
falsePositives: Treating a harmless sentence as a finding before reading the next line.
Assuming bribery, corruption, violence, or threat from a single vague sentence.
Ignoring later clarification that changes the meaning.
Missing scene-level context that explains the line.
exceptions: Context must be evaluated before judgment.
A later sentence may reverse the meaning of an earlier sentence.
Ambiguous language must not become an automatic finding.

examples.text:
هذا ظرف بسيط.
وافق على الترخيص.
examples.result: Possible bribery because the later sentence changes the meaning of the first sentence.
Weapon concept strengthened because the second sentence gives the first sentence a harmful meaning.
Possible corruption because the later line suggests a hidden arrangement.
No bribery because the later sentence does not support a corrupt meaning.

examples.text:
يخرج من السيارة حاملاً حقيبة.
يبدأ تصنيع العبوة.
examples.result: Explosive preparation because the scene description and later action combine into one harmful interpretation.

counterExamples.text: Treat a single harmless sentence as conclusive evidence.
counterExamples.reason: Later context may completely change the meaning.

counterExamples.text: Ignore the next sentence because the first sentence sounds neutral.
counterExamples.reason: Evidence must be read across the exchange.

counterExamples.text: Assume bribery from any mention of an object.
counterExamples.reason: Objects require supporting dialogue or action.

reviewerQuestions: Does later dialogue change the meaning?
Does the ending reverse the meaning?
Would this sentence alone justify a finding?

exercises.prompt: Read two consecutive lines and explain why the second line changes the meaning of the first.
exercises.expectedOutcome: The reviewer should connect the lines before deciding.

exercises.prompt: Identify whether an object mentioned in one sentence becomes harmful when paired with a later action.
exercises.expectedOutcome: The reviewer should evaluate the object in cross-sentence context.

decisionTree.question: Does the sentence need surrounding context?
Do later sentences change the meaning?
Do actions, objects, or narration confirm the interpretation?

commonMistakes: Missing the meaning created by the whole scene.

reportTemplate.reasonTemplate: The finding is supported by multiple sentences and scene context.
reportTemplate.recommendationTemplate: Reviewer should evaluate the full exchange before finalizing the finding.

confidenceGuidance.95: Dialogue, action, objects, and intent all align.
confidenceGuidance.60: Context supports the interpretation but some ambiguity remains.
confidenceGuidance.40: Only one sentence or weak corroboration exists.
confidenceGuidance.0: No reliable finding can be made.
